voice.tone: Plain and factual, allergic to hype. Claims lean on specific numbers (431,000 more pageviews, 27%, 30 days) rather than adjectives, and privacy/simplicity are treated as the default, not a selling point to oversell.
voice.rhythm: Short declarative sentences, often just two per paragraph: state the fact, then state the consequence or next step. Headers carry the setup; the sentence underneath does the explaining in one or two breaths.
voice.person: Writes as "we" for the company's own actions (what we collect, what we help with) and refers to the product by its own name, "Simple Analytics," in third person when narrating what it does or what a customer did with it. No individual signer appears in the material.
exemplars: Run Simple Analytics alongside GA4 for 30 days, free. We help you set it up and compare the numbers.

Hebban ran Simple Analytics next to GA4 and compared the reported pageview totals. Simple Analytics counted about 431,000 more pageviews, 27% more than GA4. The gap can come from consent rejection, blocking or differences in implementation.
We don't collect, store, or process personal data. That fundamentally reduces risk.
We retain data only as long as necessary to provide our service. Customers have full control and can export or delete their data at any time.

objections.objection: We already run GA4 and a consent banner that works well enough — why add and maintain a second analytics script?
objections.answer: It's positioned as additive, not a replacement: buyers keep GA4 and the consent banner and add an independent, consent-free count to compare against it, with a free 30-day period where Simple Analytics helps with setup and the comparison.

objections.objection: Pricing scales with pageviews and per extra user, so at our volume this could get expensive and we won't know the real number until well into signup.
objections.answer: The inputs are disclosed up front — a slider from the €20/month, ~100k-pageview base up to 2.5M pageviews, plus a flat +€20/month per extra user — but no price ceiling or spend guarantee appears anywhere in the pricing material.

objections.objection: Our security or procurement review will flag that SOC 2 Type II isn't finished yet.
objections.answer: The company states plainly that SOC 2 Type II is still in progress, not completed, and leans on EU hosting, Netherlands-only processing, and GDPR-by-design (because no personal data is processed) as the current story — real, but not a substitute for a finished SOC 2 report.

objections.objection: I could just keep using free GA4 instead of paying for another dashboard.
objections.answer: There's a free-forever tier (1 user, 5 sites, 1-month history, badge required), and every signup — free or paid — gets a full 14-day trial with no credit card required, so trying it costs nothing even before a paid plan is on the table.

objections.objection: We need city or region-level geo data and consistent country accuracy; this only infers country from browser timezone.
objections.answer: Nothing in the material resolves this favorably: the documentation itself admits detection is country-level only, that a few timezones are missing or shared across borders so some visitors get tagged under the wrong country, and that there is no city or region data.

objections.objection: Our reporting, audiences and conversion tracking already live in GA4 — switching is a bigger lift than the pitch suggests.
objections.answer: Enterprise positioning doesn't ask for a switch: it's described as adding campaign comparisons against GA4-reported traffic and API/BI access so existing reporting tools keep working, consistent with the (inferred) pattern that enterprise customers mainly use it to supplement GA4 rather than replace it — but no ledger evidence directly confirms this for a named enterprise customer.
